headline: Bitcoin options traders target $72K ahead of next week's Fed meeting
summary: Crypto drifted higher on Sunday with Bitcoin up 1% and Ethereum up 1.2%, but the real story is positioning ahead of the Federal Reserve's meeting later this month. Large options bets targeting $72,000 for Bitcoin by month-end have drawn attention, suggesting some traders expect the Fed's tone to be a catalyst. Fear & Greed sits at 28 — firmly in fear territory — so the optimism is cautious at best.

whyItMoved:
The top-15 moved in a narrow band today — most assets gained between 0.1% and 1.7%, with nothing dramatic in either direction. The Fear & Greed index at 28 reflects a market that is cautious despite the green numbers on screen; small gains in a fear environment often reflect thin weekend volume rather than conviction buying.

The day's most notable story is not price action but positioning. Large Bitcoin call spreads — options bets structured to pay out if Bitcoin reaches $72,000 by month-end — have been placed in size, according to CoinDesk. The timing is deliberate: the Federal Reserve meets at the end of July, and some traders appear to be wagering that a dovish signal from the Fed could push Bitcoin through that level. At $64,610, Bitcoin would need to gain roughly 11% in under two weeks for those bets to pay off — a stretch, but not an unprecedented one.

Hyperliquid led the top-15 with a 2.67% gain; no specific catalyst was reported. Solana added 1.69%. Ondo, which does not appear in the top-15 tracked list, was the session's biggest decliner at -4.39%, though no specific news event explained the move. Rain gained 3.42% with no identifiable catalyst.
worthKnowing: France ordered internet service providers to block Polymarket, the prediction market platform, in a move that could affect access for French users and raises questions about regulatory reach over decentralized platforms.

A survey cited by CoinDesk found that 84% of financial firms now treat tokenization — converting real-world assets like bonds or real estate into blockchain-based tokens — as a strategic priority, up from a minority position just two years ago.

Bitcoin's next governance debate is taking shape around 'DOG Mode,' a proposal that could affect how protocol changes are approved; details remain early-stage but the discussion is drawing attention from developers.
